methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The Live Sports Commentator
content: Problem: Students often forget the spelling rules for adding "-ing" (e.g., doubling consonants in running, dropping 'e' in scoring) and struggle to speak continuously.

Solution: We turn the classroom into a "Live Sports Channel". Students act as sports commentators. Because sports happen in real-time, the Present Continuous (am / is / are + V-ing) is the only natural tense to use. TPR involves mimicking the sports actions (kicking an imaginary ball, cheering for a win) while emphasizing the "-ing" spelling rules during writing tasks.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Toss a soft ball to a student. Ask: "What are you doing?" Student: "I am catching the ball."
S2 pull-out: Show a scoreboard where Team A has 10 points and Team B has 2. Ask: "Who is winning?" Student: "Team A is winning. Team B is losing."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). Student A has half the sports scene. Student B has the other. They ask "What is Max doing?" to complete the live report.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W16: kick, throw, catch, hit, score
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (kick, throw, catch, hit, score) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Present Continuous with sports verbs
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Present Continuous with sports verbs.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Community & Routines — Sports Commentary"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Community & Routines — Sports Commentary".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (kick, throw, catch, hit, score usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.
